## LEBANON — profile (page 182)
- Header facts: Region: Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan; income group: Lower-middle-income; lending category: IBRD; data status: Estimated data (E); population: 5.8 million; GNI: 25,704; unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- Total external debt stock, 2025: 69,294; change from 2024: +3.0%.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25: 68,232 (2015) to 69,294 (2025). The line rises from 2015 to a peak around 2018 (≈ highest point), then declines through about 2021, stays broadly flat at a lower level in 2021–24 with a slight dip and recovery, and increases in 2025.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 69,294
  - Public & publicly guaranteed: 34,715
  - Private nonguaranteed: 13,338
  - Short-term: 21,241

  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type: 34,715
    - Multilateral: 2,978
      - World Bank-IBRD: 1,191
      - IMF-SDR allocations: 1,096
      - Other multilateral: 691
    - Bilateral: 351
      - Kuwait: 229
      - Saudi Arabia: 41
      - Other bilateral: 80
    - Private creditors: 31,386

- Figure 3 Debt ratios:
  - External debt / exports: 523%; change: -7.9%. Trend: broadly stable early on, sharp rise to a peak around 2020–21, then decline, ending slightly lower in 2025.
  - External debt / GNI: 262%; change: -21.7%. Trend: broadly flat in earlier years, then strong rise to a peak around 2022–23, followed by decline to 2024. Note: no data values after 2024.
  - Debt service / exports: 14%; change: -38.6%. Trend: rises to a peak around 2020, then falls steeply, with a small bump before declining again by 2025.
  - Debt service / GNI: 10%; change: -52.9%. Trend: gradual rise to a peak around 2020–21, then sustained decline to 2024. Note: no data values after 2024.

- Figure 4 Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:
  - Official creditors:
    - Maturity: 24 yrs
    - Grace period: 7 yrs
    - Interest rate: 5.6%
  - Private creditors:
    - Maturity: ..
    - Grace period: ..
    - Interest rate: ..

- Notes:
  - Note: Figure 3 shows no data values for the GNI-based ratios after 2024.
  - Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
- Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
